pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Remove reference to DuckDB

**Why do we need this feature?**

See the blog post describing the vulnerability, for which a fix was rolled out to all Grafana versions earlier today:
https://grafana.com/blog/2024/10/17/grafana-security-release-critical-severity-fix-for-cve-2024-9264/

The full extent of our documentation around this feature seems to be here:
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/81666/files#diff-16fb71b28e5b6197615abba8a07bc73d9bf75ebc60311663e1c29976de5cc9a6

All we've documented is that the feature-flag exists. That flag still exists in the codebase, so I'm tempted not to touch that documentation for now. We can always follow up with more improvements after this PR.

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

This moves the security fix into Grafana repo itself, now that it has been publicly announced. We need this here so we can clean up and simplify our Security-releases pipeline once again.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
   Behaviour of this patch was already verified manually by @toddtreece. See his confirmation of this on our private slack, [here](https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C07P60RBAUD/p1727902629844259?thread_ts=1727901896.911799&cid=C07P60RBAUD)
   Tested again on the Ephemeral instance here: https://ephemeral1511182194942samjewe.grafana-dev.net/d/be18gem24w2dcf/test-sql-expressions-bugfix?from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: ServerSideExpressions: Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability

raw_findings.body: The documentation continues to advertise a capability that the patch removes; enabled SQL expression queries are instead rejected as not implemented.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Users are given stale configuration guidance and cannot obtain the documented behavior.
raw_findings.impact: The documentation continues to advertise a capability that the patch removes; enabled SQL expression queries are instead rejected as not implemented.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch removes the DuckDB implementation while leaving the feature-toggle documentation describing DuckDB SQL expressions unchanged.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the `sqlExpressions` feature-toggle documentation to state that SQL expressions are disabled/unsupported (or remove the toggle's documented entry if it is being retired).
raw_findings.title: Update feature-toggle documentation after removing DuckDB SQL expressions
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator reads the documented `sqlExpressions` toggle and enables it expecting SQL and DuckDB functions to be available.

raw_findings.body: There is no automated test protecting the security-critical invariant that SQL queries are rejected even when the flag is enabled, so an unintended re-enablement can reach production without CI detecting it.
raw_findings.evidence: return eq, fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")
raw_findings.failure_mode: The intended security mitigation is unverified and regressions in the rejection behavior are not caught by tests.
raw_findings.impact: There is no automated test protecting the security-critical invariant that SQL queries are rejected even when the flag is enabled, so an unintended re-enablement can reach production without CI detecting it.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces a hard-disable branch for SQL expressions without adding coverage for its enabled-toggle path.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add reader tests that submit a SQL expression with `FlagSqlExpressions` both enabled and disabled and assert that `ReadQuery` returns an error and no SQL command; include the expected rejection message or error class.
raw_findings.title: Add regression coverage for the hard SQL-expression rejection
raw_findings.trigger: A future change refactors the feature-toggle check or restores SQL command construction; the `sqlExpressions` flag is enabled in configuration.

finding.verifier_reason: The candidate claims there is no test coverage for the SQL rejection behavior, but this is a test gap suggestion rather than a defect introduced by the patch. The patch correctly adds the rejection logic at line 131. The absence of tests is a pre-existing pattern (existing tests in reader_test.go don't cover SQL expressions either). Additionally, the enableSqlExpressions function at lines 194-200 always returns false regardless of the flag state, making the 'security-critical invariant' claim about flag-based re-enablement unrealistic given the current implementation.
